parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating.

$$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{CaO(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

Table 4.1 shows the values of the Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, for this reaction at various temperatures.

Table 4.1

| $T/\text{K}$ | $\Delta G^{\ominus}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1050 | 9.9 |
| 1085 | 4.3 |
| 1120 | $-1.3$ |
| 1148 | $-5.8$ |
| 1176 | $-10.3$ |

Assume the standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$, and the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^{\ominus}$, for this reaction remain constant over this temperature range.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Use the data in Table 4.1 to plot a graph of $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ against $T$ on the grid.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the gradient of your graph. Determine the $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ in $\text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ for this reaction. Show all working.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (b)(i)

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The thermal stability of Group 1 hydrogencarbonates increases down the group.

Suggest an explanation for the trend in thermal stability of the Group 1 hydrogencarbonates.
